title: The Psychology Behind The Traitors: Trust, Lies & Human Behaviour - with Dr Ellie

sentences.en: Sometimes we get so used to doing things a certain way that we forget there might be other possibilities.
sentences.zh: 有时候我们太习惯于用某种特定的方式做事，以至于忘记了可能还有其他的可能性。

sentences.en: That can most definitely apply to our working lives too.
sentences.zh: 这绝对也适用于我们的工作生活。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent and one of the biggest changes I've made in my career has been exploring ways to earn money beyond traditional one-to-one work.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，我职业生涯中做出的最大改变之一，就是探索通过传统一对一工作之外的方式来赚钱。

sentences.zh: 经常性收入挑战”将于11月2日开始。

sentences.en: I'd love you to join us.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意你能加入我们。

sentences.en: You'll find my link in the show notes or you can drop me a DM via socials.
sentences.zh: 你可以在节目简介中找到我的链接，或者通过社交媒体给我发私信。

sentences.en: Now on with the show.
sentences.zh: 现在开始我们的节目。

sentences.en: The Traitors is a game about lies but underneath the twists, betrayals and banishments lies a much more interesting psychological question.
sentences.zh: 《叛徒》是一个关于谎言的游戏，但在反转、背叛和驱逐的表象之下，隐藏着一个更有趣的心理学问题。

sentences.en: Why are humans so fascinated by truth and why are we often so bad at recognising it?
sentences.zh: 为什么人类对真相如此着迷，又为什么我们常常这么不擅长识别它？

sentences.en: Today I'm joined by psychologist Dr. Ellie Buckley whose time on the traitors offered a front row seat to trust suspicion and human behaviour.
sentences.zh: 今天做客节目的心理学家埃利·巴克利博士，在《叛徒》的节目中亲历了信任、怀疑与人类行为。

sentences.en: Together we're exploring why our brains decide who to trust so quickly, why confidence can fool us and whether we're anywhere near as good at spotting the truth as we think we are.
sentences.zh: 我们将共同探讨，为什么我们的大脑能如此迅速地决定该信任谁，为什么自信会迷惑我们，以及我们在发现真相方面是否真如自己想象的那么厉害。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent and this is Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，这里是“心理学其实不然”。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听“心理学其实不然”。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologist and if you're watching on YouTube you might well recognise the face of the lady I'm joined by today.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特，一名合格的临床心理学家。如果你在YouTube上观看，你很可能会认出今天和我一起录节目的这位女士的面孔。

sentences.en: We have got Dr. Ellie Buckley who you might recognise from Traitors UK fame.
sentences.zh: 我们请到了埃利·巴克利博士，你可能从英国版《叛徒》中认识她。

sentences.en: Hi Faithful.
sentences.zh: 嗨，忠实者们。

sentences.en: Hi Ellie.
sentences.zh: 嗨，埃利。

sentences.en: Hi, really pleased to be here.
sentences.zh: 嗨，很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So lovely to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: Could you tell us a little bit about yourself Ellie?
sentences.zh: 埃利，能跟我们简单介绍一下你自己吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So I am a Chartered PsychologiSt. My background is predominantly academic.
sentences.zh: 我是一名特许心理学家。我的背景主要在学术界。

sentences.en: I have a PhD in Psychology where I looked at autistic people's experiences of work in the art
sentences.zh: 我拥有心理学博士学位，研究方向是自闭症人群在艺术领域的

sentences.en: and I now work in consulting where I do a mix of organisational psychology, user research with a focus on accessibility and inclusion.
sentences.zh: 工作经历。我现在从事咨询工作，主要结合组织心理学和用户研究，重点关注无障碍与包容性。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Very succinct.
sentences.zh: 非常精炼。

sentences.en: And I cannot have been the only psychologist in the country that when watching episode one saw Ellie, psychologist, and was like
sentences.zh: 而且我肯定不是全国唯一一个在看第一集时看到埃利——心理学家时觉得

sentences.en: amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了的人。

sentences.en: So yeah, well done for flying the flag for UK psychologists.
sentences.zh: 所以，干得漂亮，为英国心理学家争光了。

sentences.en: It was lovely to see you there.
sentences.zh: 很高兴在那里看到你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So I thought it might be a little bit of fun to kind of pay homage to the fact that you're on the Traitors and think today about the psychology of trust and judgment.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，为了向你参加《叛徒》节目致敬，今天探讨一下信任和判断的心理学，应该会挺有意思的。

sentences.en: And before we kick off to the main content of the episode, I thought if we could have a little bit of a quickfire round about the
sentences.zh: 在切入本期节目的主要内容之前，我想我们可以针对《叛徒》

sentences.en: Traitors.
sentences.zh: 进行一个快速问答环节。

sentences.en: And obviously if you can't comment, you're allowed to say no comment in case the BBC are watching.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你不能发表评论，以防BBC在看，你可以说“无可奉告”。

sentences.en: But yeah, it might be just a really nice way of thinking a little bit about the truths of
sentences.zh: 但这也可能是一个非常好的方式，来思考一下《叛徒》节目中

sentences.en: Traitors.
sentences.zh: 的真相。

sentences.en: So shall we get started?
sentences.zh: 那我们开始吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, let's go.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们开始。

sentences.en: So is Claudia as fabulous as we all want her to be?
sentences.zh: 克劳迪娅像我们大家希望的那样迷人吗？

sentences.en: She is more fabulous.
sentences.zh: 她比想象中还要迷人。

sentences.en: Like she's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 她简直太棒了。

sentences.en: She is so nice.
sentences.zh: 她人非常好。

sentences.en: She made the time to speak to all of us and she knew our names and just just a wonderful woman.
sentences.zh: 她专门抽出时间跟我们每个人说话，还知道我们的名字，真的是个极好的女人。

sentences.en: Like honestly, she deserves all her success.
sentences.zh: 说实话，她配得上她所有的成功。

sentences.en: Oh, well, that makes me like her even more.
sentences.zh: 哦，这让我更喜欢她了。

sentences.en: And how about the fringe?
sentences.zh: 那她的刘海呢？

sentences.en: Is that as good as we want it to be?
sentences.zh: 有我们希望的那么完美吗？

sentences.en: It's glossy.
sentences.zh: 很有光泽。

sentences.en: It's flowing.
sentences.zh: 很飘逸。

sentences.en: I don't know how she gets it so smooth.
sentences.zh: 我不知道她是怎么把它弄得那么顺滑的。

sentences.en: But yeah, it's real.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，那是真的。

sentences.en: I think she's probably got a full time fringe consultants, you know, ready to tweak at any given moment.
sentences.zh: 我想她可能有一个全职的刘海顾问，你知道的，随时准备进行修整。

sentences.en: I love that answer.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个回答。

sentences.en: Okay, next question.
sentences.zh: 好的，下一个问题。

sentences.en: What part of Traitors feels most different when you're in the moment than it does on TV?
sentences.zh: 身处现场时，《叛徒》的哪个部分感觉与在电视上看到的有最大不同？

sentences.en: Oh, that's difficult.
sentences.zh: 哦，这很难说。

sentences.en: I mean, the round table, the round table is a lot more intense than it looks.
sentences.zh: 我是说，圆桌会议，圆桌会议比看起来要紧张得多。

sentences.en: You're in there for longer than you might see on the TV.
sentences.zh: 你在里面待的时间比你在电视上看到的要长。

sentences.en: And I think especially for me, it definitely can feel quite confrontational until you settle in.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，特别是对我来说，在适应之前，它确实感觉相当具有对抗性。

sentences.en: And so it takes a few round tables for like, for at least for me to relax and go, okay, we're not having an argument.
sentences.zh: 所以需要经历几次圆桌会议，至少对我来说，我才能放松下来，告诉自己，好的，我们不是在吵架。

sentences.en: We're just, we're just playing a game.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在，只是在玩游戏。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah, those are, they look, they look long, and potentially hot and, and stressful.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些会议看起来很漫长，而且可能又热又压力山大。

sentences.en: Yeah, that looks really like a tricky aspect of Traitors.
sentences.zh: 是的，那看起来确实是《叛徒》中很棘手的一个方面。

sentences.en: All right, next question.
sentences.zh: 好的，下一个问题。

sentences.en: I am such an early to bed kind of girl.
sentences.zh: 我是一个超级喜欢早睡的女孩。

sentences.en: The idea of staying up till 12 to leave the castle or do my murdering fills me with horror.
sentences.zh: 一想到要熬夜到12点离开城堡去执行谋杀，我就感到恐惧。

sentences.en: Is it actually 12 o'clock?
sentences.zh: 真的是12点吗？

sentences.en: Or is it like a fake TV 12 o'clock?
sentences.zh: 还是电视节目里那种假的12点？

sentences.en: Or can you not say?
sentences.zh: 还是说你不能透露？

sentences.en: I can't really get into the details of the timings of the show.
sentences.zh: 我不能透露节目的具体时间安排。

sentences.en: But they were very full on days.
sentences.zh: 但那确实是非常充实的日子。

sentences.en: And we were tired.
sentences.zh: 而且我们很累。

sentences.en: And what I will say, is that it's you think you're going to have enough time to when you're going to bed to kind of mull over the day and think about what you learn that
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，你以为在上床睡觉时会有足够的时间来回味这一天，想想你那天学到了什么

sentences.en: day and what to bring in the next day.
sentences.zh: 以及第二天要带什么进城堡。

sentences.en: And actually, I was so zonked out.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我当时累得不省人事。

sentences.en: I was like, I better get my sleep just so I'm ready for tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我心想：我最好抓紧睡觉，好为明天做好准备。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember watching the Celebrity Traitors.
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得我看过名人版《叛徒》。

sentences.en: And then one of the traitors was having a nap and then was accused of being overly tired because she was, because she was asleep in the day.
sentences.zh: 然后其中一个叛徒在打盹，接着就被指控过度疲劳，因为她在白天睡着了。

sentences.en: And she was just like, No, it's because I'm autistic.
sentences.zh: 她当时就说：“不，那是因为我有自闭症。”

sentences.en: And I've got ADHD.
sentences.zh: “而且我有ADHD。”

sentences.en: And I need to ask that that is the best answer.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，这是最好的回答。

sentences.en: I was like, Kat, you're naughty.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想：凯特，你太调皮了。

sentences.en: Famously, you and your boyfriend Ross went into the castle as a secret couple.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你和你的男友罗斯作为秘密情侣进入了城堡。

sentences.en: I think I would struggle to not call my husband babe and to be really over familiar with him.
sentences.zh: 我想我会很难不叫我丈夫“宝贝”，也很难不对他表现得过于亲密。

sentences.en: How on earth did you?
sentences.zh: 你到底是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Did you begin to get your heads around that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么开始适应这一点的？

sentences.en: Well, it was really challenging.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很有挑战性。

sentences.en: I was definitely really, really nervous around Ross.
sentences.zh: 我在罗斯身边时绝对非常非常紧张。

sentences.en: And he actually told me afterwards, he thought I was a traitor because I was behaving so weirdly.
sentences.zh: 他事后甚至告诉我，他以为我是叛徒，因为我的行为太古怪了。

sentences.en: My strategy, essentially, was just to avoid him in the castle.
sentences.zh: 我的策略基本上就是，在城堡里尽量避开他。

sentences.en: So actually, if you watch those first few episodes, you're not going to see us in many shots together, because every time he entered a room, I would just leave it.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，如果你看前几集，你会发现我们一起出镜的镜头并不多，因为他每次进房间，我都会立刻离开。

sentences.en: And well, I mean, luckily or unluckily for us, there was a lot of other distraction.
sentences.zh: 而且，对我们来说幸运或不幸的是，当时有很多其他的干扰。

sentences.en: He had another friend in the castle.
sentences.zh: 他在城堡里还有另一个朋友。

sentences.en: And so ultimately, we didn't have much time to accidentally call each other babe before it all went wrong anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，在一切出岔子之前，我们根本没有太多时间不小心叫对方宝贝。

sentences.en: Oh, I love that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, just as soon as you see him, like Ellie just like left the room.
sentences.zh: 是的，只要你看到他，埃利就会直接离开房间。

sentences.en: That's hilarious.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Another one about Ross.
sentences.zh: 另一个关于罗斯的问题。

sentences.en: How enough did you manage to to not cry or not scream?
sentences.zh: 你到底是怎么做到不哭也不尖叫的？

sentences.en: No, when when Ross were voted out?
sentences.zh: 不，我是说罗斯被投票出局的时候？

sentences.en: Do you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: We'd got ready.
sentences.zh: 我们已经做好了心理准备。

sentences.en: We'd obviously we knew we were going on the show before we got there.
sentences.zh: 我们去之前当然就知道我们要参加这个节目。

sentences.en: And so we discussed all the potential scenarios that could happen.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论了所有可能发生的潜在情况。

sentences.en: And because of that, he had basically a first meeting on the driveway with an old friend.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，他基本上在车道上就和老朋友进行了第一次见面。

sentences.en: And we knew that that was going to be bad.
sentences.zh: 我们知道那会是个糟糕的开始。

sentences.en: And so I was like, right, this isn't going to go well.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想：好吧，这下不妙了。

sentences.en: He's probably not going to survive this.
sentences.zh: 他可能挺不过这一关了。

sentences.en: So I'd kind of braced myself from day one.
sentences.zh: 所以我从第一天起就做好了心理准备。

sentences.en: He's probably going to go.
sentences.zh: 他可能要被淘汰了。

sentences.en: So I held it in.
sentences.zh: 所以我克制住了。

sentences.en: I did want to cry.
sentences.zh: 我当然想哭。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对想哭。

sentences.en: But I was also like, I've got to do this.
sentences.zh: 但我也告诉自己：我必须坚持下去。

sentences.en: I've got to do this for the both of us.
sentences.zh: 我得为了我们俩坚持下去。

sentences.en: Hold it together.
sentences.zh: 稳住。

sentences.en: Don't ruin the game.
sentences.zh: 别搞砸了游戏。

sentences.en: Like if he's already out, don't be the one who then gets both of us out at the same time.
sentences.zh: 如果他已经出局了，千万别做那个让咱们俩同时被淘汰的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd forgotten about that little weird twiSt. And I presume that was entirely random.
sentences.zh: 对，我差点忘了那个奇怪的小插曲。我猜那是完全随机的吧？

sentences.en: Like of all the people in the UK, how could you know that you're going to meet someone that you've, I think, previously worked with?
sentences.zh: 在英国所有人当中，你怎么会知道自己会遇到一个你以前可能合作过的人？

sentences.en: Like very small world.
sentences.zh: 世界真是太小了。

sentences.en: Yeah, very much so.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: And we were not expecting that at all.
sentences.zh: 而且我们完全没有料到这一点。

sentences.en: So it really threw a spanner in the works.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的打乱了我们的计划。

sentences.en: Yeah, and probably ultimately led to his untimely early exit, I would say.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我想这最终导致了他过早被淘汰出局。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, very much so.
sentences.zh: 对，对，确实如此。

sentences.en: I think what he found really frustrating was initially when he saw his friend, he thought, maybe I have a super advantage.
sentences.zh: 我想他觉得最沮丧的是，一开始看到朋友时，他心想：也许我有超级优势。

sentences.en: I've actually got two allies in this game.
sentences.zh: 我在这个游戏里实际上有两个盟友。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, Nettie was so excited.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，内蒂太兴奋了。

sentences.en: She called out to him in front of everyone.
sentences.zh: 她在所有人面前大声喊他。

sentences.en: And obviously, you know, the traitors will pick up on anything to try and influence the game.
sentences.zh: 显然，你知道的，叛徒会抓住任何事情来试图影响游戏局势。

sentences.en: So it was an easy way to kind of make everyone focus on them.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个让所有人把注意力集中在他们身上的好方法。

sentences.en: So an easy way to lose trust in who they knew was a faithful and to make themselves look gloriously golden.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种轻易失去对一个已知是忠实者的人的信任，并让自己显得光芒四射的好方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, very much.
sentences.zh: 对，确实如此。

sentences.en: Do you film solidly for days and weeks on end?
sentences.zh: 你们是一连好几天甚至好几周都在连续拍摄吗？

sentences.en: Or do you get some days off to decompress?
sentences.zh: 还是说会有几天休息时间来放松调整？

sentences.en: Yeah, I can't get too much into the filming schedule.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不能透露太多拍摄日程。

sentences.en: But we are really well looked after there are down days where we can kind of recuperate.
sentences.zh: 但我们在那里被照顾得很好，有休息日可以让我们恢复体力。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 那就好。

sentences.en: I'm pleased to hear it.
sentences.zh: 听到这个我很高兴。

sentences.en: Because I just think it's a lot to manage all those different parts, as well as just being your normal human self as well.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得要应对所有这些不同的部分，还要表现得像个正常人，真的要处理很多事情。

sentences.en: Are you allowed to text your mom?
sentences.zh: 你们可以给妈妈发短信吗？

sentences.en: Or is there like no phones available?
sentences.zh: 还是说根本没有手机可用？

sentences.en: No, no devices, no phones, you have no contact with the outside world while you're in the castle.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有设备，没有手机，你在城堡里时与外界没有任何联系。

sentences.en: Oh, so you had to get a bit analog then and kind of really think about, you know, me, myself and I.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以你们不得不回归一点模拟时代的生活，真正去思考自己内心深处的想法？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that's possibly what I found quite challenging about the game as well, is I'm used to working things out through conversation.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得这也可能是我觉得这个游戏相当具有挑战性的地方，因为我习惯了通过对话来理清思绪。

sentences.en: Like I will go to Ross or someone else to talk through my thoughts and sound them out.
sentences.zh: 比如我会去找罗斯或其他人倾诉我的想法，把它们顺一顺。

sentences.en: And actually sounding things out just with yourself, you kind of get caught in a spiral sometimes.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果只是自己一个人反复琢磨，有时你就会陷入一种恶性循环。

sentences.en: And you're like, I don't know if
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，我不知道

sentences.en: I'm correct.
sentences.zh: 我到底猜得对不对。

sentences.en: If I'm not, I need a sounding board.
sentences.zh: 如果不确定的话，我需要一个人来帮我参谋参谋。

sentences.en: And I didn't have one.
sentences.zh: 而我当时没有这样一个人。

sentences.en: Okay, so being alone is just like being in an echo chamber where you're just like, no, I've had this theory already.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以独自一人就像置身于回音室里，你会觉得，不对，我之前就已经有过这个理论了。

sentences.en: That's not going to work.
sentences.zh: 那个行不通的。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: Other than Ross, have you stayed in touch with anyone?
sentences.zh: 除了罗斯，你还和谁保持着联系吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，当然有。

sentences.en: Like we've all got the group WhatsApp.
sentences.zh: 比如我们所有人都在一个WhatsApp群里。

sentences.en: And then I see some of the players every now and then.
sentences.zh: 然后我时不时还会见到一些其他的玩家。

sentences.en: We were really lucky to see Harriet recently.
sentences.zh: 我们最近真的很幸运见到了哈丽特。

sentences.en: She's a good friend.
sentences.zh: 她是个很好的朋友。

sentences.en: And then we see Jade sometimes as well.
sentences.zh: 然后我们有时也会见到杰德。

sentences.en: And Jessie.
sentences.zh: 还有杰西。

sentences.en: So yeah, we stayed in touch.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们一直保持着联系。

sentences.en: And I love how much it's kind of transformed Stephen and Stephen's career and some of the stuff he's getting to do because of his flamboyant outfits, basically.
sentences.zh: 而且我特别喜欢这档节目在很大程度上改变了斯蒂芬以及斯蒂芬的职业生涯，还有他现在能做的一些事情，基本上都是因为他那些张扬的穿着。

sentences.en: Did you have to have a think about what am I going to wear on camera like every day?
sentences.zh: 你是不是每天都得琢磨一下：我今天在镜头前要穿什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: I had a think.
sentences.zh: 我确实琢磨过。

sentences.en: And I was like, you know, it's funny when you're going on a show like this and you're like, I want to have fun, but I also want to maintain
sentences.zh: 我就在想，你知道的，当你参加这样一个节目时，那种感觉挺逗的，一方面你想玩得开心，但另一方面我也想保持

sentences.en: some professionalism because I've got a career.
sentences.zh: 一定的专业性，因为我毕竟有自己的职业。

sentences.en: And, and so I was like, how do I dress in a way that I'm like, you know, I'm serious enough.
sentences.zh: 所以我就在想，我该怎么穿才能既显得……你知道的，足够严谨。

sentences.en: I don't know if I got it quite right.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我当时有没有拿捏得刚刚好。

sentences.en: But also it was like, I didn't have the budget to go and buy a bunch of new clothes.
sentences.zh: 但同时我也觉得，我并没有那么多预算去买一堆新衣服。

sentences.en: So I was like,
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就想：

sentences.en: I've just got to pull from what I've got and we'll just make it work.
sentences.zh: 我只能从现有的衣服里挑，然后凑合着把这事儿搞定就行了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I guess even going forwards, brands are not necessarily going to be able to work with contestants because it's all really cloak and dagger, so to speak, about who's going in.
sentences.zh: 而且我猜，哪怕放眼未来，品牌方也不一定能和参赛选手合作，因为关于谁会去参加节目，可以说是高度保密的，也就是所谓的机密。

sentences.en: So yeah, maybe start curating your own.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，也许你在购物时就可以开始筹备你自己的

sentences.en: If I'm on traders, this is what I'm going to wear wardrobe when you're shopping.
sentences.zh: “如果我上了《叛徒》我该穿什么”的专属衣橱了。

sentences.en: Ultimately, Stephen's wardrobe was really effective.
sentences.zh: 说到底，斯蒂芬的衣橱真的非常有效。

sentences.en: He even referenced the idea that he'd wear a more flamboyant outfit on a day where he was under suspicion to draw attention to the outfit rather than everything else.
sentences.zh: 他甚至还提到过这样一个想法：在那些他受到怀疑的日子里，他会穿一套更加张扬的衣服，以此来把大家的注意力吸引到衣服上，而不是其他事情上。

sentences.en: And I thought that was a great idea.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个主意棒极了。

sentences.en: That really is a good strategy.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个好策略。

sentences.en: By the end of filming, do you feel like you trusted your instincts more or less?
sentences.zh: 到拍摄结束时，你觉得你对自己的直觉是更信任了还是更不信任了？

sentences.en: Less.
sentences.zh: 更不信任了。

sentences.en: Less.
sentences.zh: 更不信任了。

sentences.en: I was completely lost in there.
sentences.zh: 我在里面彻底迷失了。

sentences.en: I think when I found out who the traitors were,
sentences.zh: 我觉得当我发现谁是叛徒的时候，

sentences.en: I just, you know what, with Rachel, I thought she was a fantastic player, so skilled.
sentences.zh: 我只是……你知道吗，对于雷切尔，我以前觉得她是个极具天赋的玩家，能力非常强。

sentences.en: And it's really weird to watch it back and obviously see that she was made a traitor from the beginning because it was just really hard to imagine her being a traitor.
sentences.zh: 回看节目时看到她从一开始就被选为叛徒，这种感觉真的很诡异，因为你实在很难想象她会是个叛徒。

sentences.en: She was so convincing.
sentences.zh: 她伪装得太有说服力了。

sentences.en: And I thought, wow, that is such an interesting thing to learn that, you know, you really can't spot people.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，哇，了解这一点真的太有意思了，你知道的，你确实没办法看透别人。

sentences.en: And you know, I think I thought I had better intuition than I did, but a really good learning experience.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，我觉得我以前的直觉比实际要好，但这也是一次非常棒的学习经历。

sentences.en: And maybe it just illustrates that the game's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 也许这也说明了这个游戏真的很艰难。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，我也这么觉得。

sentences.en: And also it's so person specific.
sentences.zh: 而且这非常因人而异。

sentences.en: So I can tell when my eldest son lies to me because he's, I don't know, he's just got these tells that I can see.
sentences.zh: 所以我能看出我大儿子什么时候在对我说谎，因为他，怎么说呢，他有一些我能看出来的破绽。

sentences.en: My youngest son, rarely can I tell if he's lying.
sentences.zh: 至于我小儿子，我几乎很难看出他是不是在说谎。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's when I know them that well.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，明明我对他们那么了解。

sentences.en: But I was thinking, you know, partly because I messaged you during the show, and obviously, you weren't allowed to tell me anything.
sentences.zh: 但当时我在想，部分原因是因为我在节目期间给你发了信息，而且显然，你是什么都不能告诉我的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But I was like, Oh, maybe Ellie could be the secret traitor.
sentences.zh: 但我就在想：哦，也许埃莉会是那个秘密叛徒。

sentences.en: But then I was like, God, if, if a secret traitor is a psychologist who then goes on to win the show, are we going to set back
sentences.zh: 但转念一想，天哪，如果这个秘密叛徒是一位心理学家，然后她还赢了节目，那我们是不是会把

sentences.en: the trust in psychologists and mental health practitioners, you know, to the point of destruction?
sentences.zh: 公众对心理学家和心理健康从业者的信任，彻底摧毁到无可挽回的地步？

sentences.en: Can we ever come back from that?
sentences.zh: 我们还能从那种局面里恢复过来吗？

sentences.en: So I think personally,
sentences.zh: 所以我想就我个人而言，

sentences.en: I may be a little bit glad that you weren't, weren't the secret traitor.
sentences.zh: 我可能稍微有点庆幸你不是那个秘密叛徒。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, I'm ultimately pleased there wasn't a traitor.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，归根结底我还是很高兴没有出现那种叛徒的。

sentences.en: I did ask to be a traitor.
sentences.zh: 我其实申请过当叛徒。

sentences.en: I thought it's a game.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这只是个游戏。

sentences.en: And you know, this isn't, you know, this is a game and we need to separate like, you know, how we play a game from how we operate in the real world.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，这并不是……这只是个游戏，我们需要把我们在游戏中怎么玩，和我们在现实生活中怎么做区分开来。

sentences.en: But I would have been absolutely rubbish tracer.
sentences.zh: 但我绝对会是个糟糕透顶的叛徒。

sentences.en: I actually don't have it in me.
sentences.zh: 我骨子里其实干不来这事儿。

sentences.en: I could barely be a faithful.
sentences.zh: 我连当一个忠诚者都勉勉强强。

sentences.en: I was struggling to even keep the secret of my relationship.
sentences.zh: 我甚至连隐藏自己恋情的秘密都在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: I felt so guilty.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得太内疚了。

sentences.en: So yeah, ultimately, I was a faithful at heart, even if I hadn't quite identified that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，归根结底我内心深处还是个忠诚者，哪怕我当时还没完全意识到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think I'd be the same.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得我也会是这样。

sentences.en: I think I'm, I try to be really authentic in everything I do.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我在做的所有事情中都努力保持真正的自我。

sentences.en: And so I would, I think I would have really struggled.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我当时一定会非常痛苦。

sentences.en: But also like the whole Alan Carr thing, like, even when you try and say I am a faithful, or I'm a traitor, I really think that I would
sentences.zh: 而且就像整个艾伦·卡尔梗那样，哪怕你试图去说“我是个忠诚者”或者“我是个叛徒”，我真的觉得我会

sentences.en: accidentally say I am, you know, because obviously, I'm a traitor, because even the show is called traitors.
sentences.zh: 不小心说出“我是……”你知道的，因为很显然，我是个叛徒，因为连节目的名字都叫《叛徒》。

sentences.en: It's really hard to not just say those words.
sentences.zh: 要忍住不说出这些字眼真的太难了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And we saw, I think Rachel made a verbal slip up quite late in the game.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，好像雷切尔在游戏后期出现了一次口误。

sentences.en: But ultimately, things were so deep in, actually, the players didn't notice.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，当时局势已经太深了，实际上其他玩家并没有注意到。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think it's really challenging.
sentences.zh: 不过，是的，我觉得这真的很有挑战性。

sentences.en: And yeah, saying something, you know, just just lying, it's just difficult.
sentences.zh: 而且，说点什么吧，仅仅是撒谎，本身就很困难。

sentences.en: And it's a lot of pressure you're putting on yourself.
sentences.zh: 而且你给自己施加了很大的压力。

sentences.en: Yeah, and kind of, I don't know, credit, credit to some of the players who could do that really well.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且某种程度上……怎么说呢，真得向那些能把这一点做得很好的玩家致敬。

sentences.en: You know, it's a skill.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一种技能。

sentences.en: It is a skill.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一种技能。

sentences.en: And we won't ask any more about, about their psychopathology, about why they're so good at that.
sentences.zh: 我们就不再深入探讨他们的精神病理学了，不去探究他们为什么在这方面这么厉害。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for playing my little quickfire round about the truth of traitors, Ellie.
sentences.zh: 埃莉，非常感谢你参与我这个关于“叛徒真相”的快速问答环节。

sentences.en: Let's get on with the main content of our episode.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续我们这期节目的主要内容吧。

sentences.en: So the traitors is almost social experiment in the first impressions of, of people and strangers.
sentences.zh: 所以，《叛徒》差不多算是一场关于人们和陌生人第一印象的社会实验。

sentences.en: How good do you think we are at that as humans?
sentences.zh: 你觉得作为人类，我们在这方面到底有多厉害？

sentences.en: Oh, do you know what intuition?
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道吗，关于直觉嘛……

sentences.en: It depends.
sentences.zh: 这得看情况。

sentences.en: It's always it depends.
sentences.zh: 永远都是“这得看情况”。

sentences.en: Like, we know that, you know, we make judgments very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 就像我们所知道的，我们会非常非常快地做出判断。

sentences.en: You know, in psychology, they look at things called thin slice judgments, you know, people are very quick to make a decision about what they
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在心理学中，他们会研究一种叫做“薄片判断”（thin slice judgments）的东西，你知道的，人们很快就能对一个人的

sentences.en: think about someone's going to be like, whether they're going to be friendly, or unfriendly, you know, whether they think they're going to get on with them.
sentences.zh: 为人做出决定，比如他们觉得这人会是什么样，是友好还是不友好，你知道的，觉得自个儿能不能跟对方合得来。

sentences.en: And some, some of them, we're accurate to an extent, you know, and that's to help us like decide who's a threat to us.
sentences.zh: 而且有些判断，我们在某种程度上是准确的，你知道的，这有助于我们判断谁对我们构成了威胁。

sentences.en: You know, there's a reason why we're quick to judge, but it's so prone to bias.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们习惯快速做出判断是有原因的，但这非常容易产生偏见。

sentences.en: And so we have to understand our own biases to try and consciously unpick them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须了解我们自己的偏见，以便有意识地去剖析它们。

sentences.en: Because if we don't do that, then we're going to make incorrect judgments about a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们不这么做，我们就会对许多人做出错误的判断。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I don't think I've heard the term thin slice judgments before.
sentences.zh: 我以前好像没听过“薄片判断”这个词。

sentences.en: I'm guessing the opposite would be thick slice that you've got more, more context, more awareness, longer time period.
sentences.zh: 我猜相反的词应该叫“厚片判断”吧，意味着你拥有更多的背景信息、更高的认知度以及更长的时间跨度。

sentences.en: I guess so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Do you know what, like, it's not, it's not 100% my area.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，这其实并不是我百分之百擅长的领域。

sentences.en: But as in, yeah, there's lots of experiments where essentially thin slice judgments are where participants are shown a really short clip,
sentences.zh: 不过也就是说，有很多实验基本上都是通过让参与者观看一段非常短的片段来进行薄片判断，

sentences.en: it might be a video clip, an audio clip of someone, and then they'll be asked to decide on their characteristics.
sentences.zh: 可能是一个视频片段，也可能是某人的音频片段，然后让他们据此判断对方的性格特征。

sentences.en: And they can be surprisingly accurate, you know, about kind of like some of their personality traits, other things.
sentences.zh: 而且他们在某些性格特质和其他方面，准确度可能会出奇地高。

sentences.en: But it's very prone to bias.
sentences.zh: 但它非常容易产生偏见。

sentences.en: So it's not, it's definitely not a perfect system.
sentences.zh: 所以它绝对不是一个完美的系统。

sentences.en: Yeah, that rings a bell of something I've been reading recently on psychopaths.
sentences.zh: 是的，这让我想起了我最近读到的一些关于精神病态者的内容。

sentences.en: And actually, when people are shown very short clips of people with high psychopathic traits, they are better at spotting whether they might be a psychopath or not.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当人们观看带有高精神病态特质的人的极短视频片段时，他们更能准确辨别对方是不是精神病态者。

sentences.en: When it's longer,
sentences.zh: 而当时间变长时——

sentences.en: longer for the person to poison your narrative and your kind of guesses, it's harder.
sentences.zh: 当对方有更多时间来毒害你的叙事和你的各种猜测时，事情反而变得更难了。

sentences.en: And I wonder if that's maybe what's going on in the traitors as well.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这会不会也是《叛徒》中正在发生的事情呢？

sentences.en: Like your initial thin slice judgment might then be undone by, you know, all of the wizardry, all of the puppetry of the show.
sentences.zh: 就像你最初的薄片判断，随后可能会被节目中所有的花招、所有的幕后操控给彻底瓦解。

sentences.en: Very much so, you know, and then also, you then as the game moves on, I think you then need to think
sentences.zh: 确实如此，你知道的，而且随着游戏的推进，我认为你接下来还需要考虑

sentences.en: about that kind of in group bias, your own want and desire to be part of the in group,
sentences.zh: 那种所谓的“内群体偏见”，你想要并渴望成为内群体一员的心理，

sentences.en: and to listen to the authority figures in the game and to kind of, what do you call it, but be, yeah, just be in the group, you don't want to stand out.
sentences.zh: 以及去听从游戏中那些权威人物的意见，并且……怎么说呢，就是融入群体，你不想显得格格不入。

sentences.en: And so sometimes your, your initial judgment, you might override it to try and fit in with what other people are saying as well.
sentences.zh: 所以有时你可能会推翻自己最初的判断，去迎合其他人正在说的话。

sentences.en: And I think we're all, we can all be prone to that sometimes.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我们所有人有时都容易受到这种影响。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: It's right back to our primitive brains, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这完全可以追溯到我们原始的大脑，不是吗？

sentences.en: That actually being mammals, being part of something, and not being by yourself and isolated is so important, because you're vulnerable otherwise.
sentences.zh: 事实上，作为哺乳动物，成为某个集体的一部分，而不是孤立无援地独自一人，是如此重要，因为否则你就会变得很脆弱。

sentences.en: And that crops up at all different stages of our life, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这种情况在我们生命的各个不同阶段都会出现，对吧？

sentences.en: It crops up in schools where you want to be part of something, even in workplaces, and in kind of friendship groups.
sentences.zh: 它会出现在学校里，你想成为某个集体的一部分；甚至在工作场所，以及各种朋友圈子中。

sentences.en: It's, it's everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它无处不在。

sentences.en: And it would be, you know, silly of us to think that isn't cropping up in TV shows like the Traitors.
sentences.zh: 如果我们认为这种现象不会在像《叛徒》这样的电视节目中出现，那我们就太傻了。

sentences.en: Yeah, very much.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: You were, you were literally fighting to survive in that show because you could get banished by the group every day.
sentences.zh: 你在那个节目里简直就是为了生存而战，因为你每天都可能被大家驱逐出局。

sentences.en: And so I think at that point, when you're then trying to fit in with the group, and you're, you're trying to keep
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得在那种情况下，当你试图融入群体时，当你试图保持

sentences.en: your mind open to other people's opinions and thoughts and their kind of sway, then you start to maybe go, Oh, maybe I didn't get that right.
sentences.zh: 开放的心态去接受别人的意见、想法以及他们的某种左右时，你可能就会开始觉得：哦，也许我之前没搞对。

sentences.en: I definitely got into a place where I was really doubting my own intuition, my own ability to work out things.
sentences.zh: 我当时确实陷入了一种状态，开始严重怀疑自己的直觉，怀疑自己把事情理清的能力。

sentences.en: And I was trying to listen to other people as authority figures.
sentences.zh: 我当时试图去听从其他人的意见，把他们当成权威人物。

sentences.en: And I mean, it's just, it's just an exercise in learning more about yourself and how quickly you, you place someone else up on a pedestal and listen to their opinion over your own.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是一次关于自我了解的练习，看看你有多快就会把别人高高捧上神坛，并且听信他们的意见而不是你自己的。

sentences.en: So yeah, a lot of learning.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，学到了很多东西。

sentences.en: Do you think suggestibility comes into this?
sentences.zh: 你觉得易受暗示性（suggestibility）会在这里面起作用吗？

sentences.en: Do you think any players are more likely to be suggestible and therefore more easily swayed?
sentences.zh: 你觉得有些玩家是不是更容易受到暗示，从而更容易被左右？

sentences.en: Or do you think it's just down to what happens on the day and who you end up with?
sentences.zh: 还是说你觉得这完全取决于当天的具体情况以及和你最终分到一起的人是谁？

sentences.en: Your suggestibility can change, I think, depending on the context, depending how confident you feel,
sentences.zh: 我觉得你的易受暗示性是会发生变化的，这取决于上下文环境，取决于你当时觉得有多自信，

sentences.en: depending on who you feel like the leader is in that situation, depending on how safe you feel
sentences.zh: 取决于你觉得那种情况下谁是领导者，取决于你觉得表达自己的安全感有多高——

sentences.en: to express, you know, we can think about psychological safety, like how safe do you feel to express a dissenting opinion?
sentences.zh: 我们可以想想心理安全感，比如你觉得表达异见有多安全？

sentences.en: And if you don't, do you then turn inwards and start to doubt your own feelings?
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得不安全，你是会选择内化并开始怀疑自己的感受？

sentences.en: Or do you hold it strong, even if you're not expressing?
sentences.zh: 还是会坚守己见，哪怕你没有说出口？

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think there was something around confidence, isn't there, that Stephen almost,
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我觉得这里面还涉及某种与自信有关的东西，对吧，斯蒂芬他几乎……

sentences.en: you know, detracted that attention from him, because it was just his flamboyant character.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这转移了人们对他的注意力，因为他那个人本身就很张扬。

sentences.en: And he was kind of naturally a leader.
sentences.zh: 而且他天生就有点领袖气质。

sentences.en: It felt a little bit like, you know, the big dog theory for the celebrity traitors with Stephen Fry and Jonathan Ross.
sentences.zh: 这感觉有点像是，你知道的，斯蒂芬·弗赖和乔纳森·罗斯那期名人版《反叛者》里的“大狗理论”。

sentences.en: And it felt very much like Stephen was kind of the equivalent big dog.
sentences.zh: 而且感觉斯蒂芬很像是那个对应的大狗。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think Stephen was very likable, like he worked really hard to bond with everyone, be very kind to people, complimentary.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得斯蒂芬非常讨人喜欢，他非常努力地去和每个人建立联系，对人很好，也很会赞美别人。

sentences.en: And that goes a long way, you know, in getting people to trust you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这在赢得别人对你的信任方面能起很大作用。

sentences.en: And then once you've built some trust, they then don't want to doubt you.
sentences.zh: 一旦你建立了一些信任，他们就不会想要去怀疑你了。

sentences.en: And I think that's the, that's the great thing about the game.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这就是这个游戏的精妙之处。

sentences.en: And what's so tricky is that you start to form bonds and friendships.
sentences.zh: 最棘手的是，你开始建立纽带和友谊。

sentences.en: And then you don't want to doubt your friends.
sentences.zh: 然后你就不想怀疑你的朋友了。

sentences.en: And that's where it becomes really difficult.
sentences.zh: 这就是事情变得非常困难的地方。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That's how, that's how we begin to trust people as friendships and, and, you know, live as tribes, really, that we need to be able to think that some people are trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们如何开始信任他人、建立友谊的方式，而且，你知道的，人类实际上是以部落形式生活的，我们需要能够认为某些人是值得信赖的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对如此。

sentences.en: We have to find a way through, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 我们总得找出一条路来，不是吗？

sentences.en: And we're just looking for who we can kind of assess as the most trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在寻找我们可以评估为最值得信赖的人。

sentences.en: It doesn't always mean we're right, but we're going to try.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们总是对的，但我们要去尝试。

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Do you think we sometimes mistake confidence for competence when it comes to trust?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我们在谈到信任时，有时会把自信误认为是能力吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, very much so.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常明显。

sentences.en: What I kind of understand from research is that confidence often comes from the coherence of the story that you can make rather than the actual competence.
sentences.zh: 从研究中我了解到的是，自信往往来自于你能构建的故事的连贯性，而不是实际的能力。

sentences.en: So it's like, if you can make a narrative that makes sense to you, you're much more likely to trust it.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比，如果你能编织出一个对你来说说得通的叙事，你就更有可能去相信它。

sentences.en: And that's the same if you're listening to someone else.
sentences.zh: 当你听别人说话时也是一样的。

sentences.en: If they sound coherent, you're much more likely to trust what they're saying.
sentences.zh: 如果他们听起来逻辑连贯，你就更有可能相信他们所说的话。

sentences.en: And it's not actually about whether the facts actually back it up.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上并不取决于事实是否真的支持它。

sentences.en: So yeah, that there can be a lot of confounding factors between competence and confidence.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，能力和自信之间可能会存在很多混淆因素。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: And I do think, you know, maybe Alan Carr got so far in his journey, because people already had this kind of coherent narrative of what he was like.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，你知道的，也许阿兰·卡尔在他的旅程中能走那么远，是因为人们对他是什么样的人已经有了这种连贯的叙事。

sentences.en: Whereas obviously, if he had come into the castle as a non-celebrity, just sweating profusely and, you know, being quite flamboyant, it might not have had the same outcome for him.
sentences.zh: 而显而易见的是，如果他作为一个素人走进城堡，只是一直冒汗，你知道的，表现得相当张扬，他的结局可能就不会一样了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it's essentially like, yeah, are people fitting your expectations?
sentences.zh: 这基本上就像是，人们是否符合你的预期？

sentences.en: And obviously in the civilian trades, we don't know each other.
sentences.zh: 显然，在平民版的《反叛者》中，我们并不认识彼此。

sentences.en: So we don't have expectations.
sentences.zh: 所以我们没有什么期望。

sentences.en: And that's obviously where, you know, kind of more difficult things around bias can come in.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这就是那些围绕偏见的更棘手问题可能介入的地方。

sentences.en: And, you know, what are you expecting of certain people versus other people?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你对某些人和其他人有什么样的期望？

sentences.en: But yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And then there is someone behaving consistently through the experience as well.
sentences.zh: 然后还有人在整个经历中表现得很一致的情况。

sentences.en: And, you know, Ross had picked up that actually Stephen hadn't blushed on the train when we first met him.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，罗斯发现其实斯蒂芬在我们刚见面时在火车上并没有脸红。

sentences.en: And then he was blushing through the rest of the experience.
sentences.zh: 但他却在接下来的经历中一直都在脸红。

sentences.en: So maybe, but like, obviously, Ross didn't get a chance to really put that theory out there.
sentences.zh: 所以也许，但是很显然，罗斯并没有机会真正把这个理论说出来。

sentences.en: And, you know, the traitors are picked so early, you don't really get a chance to know your fellow players very well, before everything's begun.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，反叛者选得太早了，在一切开始之前，你其实没有机会真正很好地了解你的队友。

sentences.en: And so it's really hard to pick out, like, are they meeting my expectations for a traitor versus for a faithful?
sentences.zh: 所以很难挑出来，比如，他们是符合我对反叛者的预期还是对忠诚者的预期？

sentences.en: Because people were nervous for all sorts of reasons in the game.
sentences.zh: 因为游戏里的人们会由于各种各样的原因感到紧张。

sentences.en: And lots of people were displaying, you know, nervous or slightly odd behaviour, but because of different causes.
sentences.zh: 而且很多人都表现出了，你知道的，紧张或稍微有点奇怪的行为，但这是由不同的原因引起的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think Stephen might have said, well, I wasn't wearing any synthetic fibres on the train.
sentences.zh: 对，我想斯蒂芬可能会说，嗯，我在火车上没有穿任何合成纤维的衣服。

sentences.en: And now I am.
sentences.zh: 而我现在穿了。

sentences.en: And it's really hot.
sentences.zh: 而且天气真的很热。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: Obviously, when we're looking at social judgments, we do not always get it right, do we?
sentences.zh: 很显然，当我们在做社会判断时，并不总是对的，对吧？

sentences.en: No, very much so.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: But what can be really tricky is that we don't always get feedback that we're wrong.
sentences.zh: 但非常棘手的一点是，我们并不总是能得到我们错了的反馈。

sentences.en: You know, often, if we make an incorrect judgment, no one's telling us people might secretly be thinking
sentences.zh: 你知道的，通常如果我们做出了错误的判断，没有人会告诉我们，人们可能私下里在想

sentences.en: something, but actually, it's quite rare to receive, you know, corrective feedback.
sentences.zh: 某些事，但实际上，要收到纠正性的反馈是相当罕见的。

sentences.en: And so then we can just carry on with those biases that we're carrying.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就可以带着我们原有的偏见继续下去了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think so much of what we do and what we learn and how we learn is context specific.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我认为我们的很多所作所为、我们所学到的东西以及我们的学习方式都是特定于上下文的。

sentences.en: So even when really horrendous things happen, but it's a result of a really quick impulsive accident,
sentences.zh: 所以即使是非常可怕的事情发生了，但它只是一次非常快速的冲动事故的结果，

sentences.en: or just something that you've overlooked or neglected to do that you'd usually do, you know,
sentences.zh: 或者只是你忽视了或疏忽了平时会做的事情，你知道的，

sentences.en: 99 times out of 100.
sentences.zh: 100次里有99次都会做的那种。

sentences.en: You know, people will always be in the comments, well, you know, of course, you couldn't be trusted, because you didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，评论区里总会有人说，嗯，你知道的，当然你是不值得信任的，因为你没有那样做。

sentences.en: Or, you know, you didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，你没有做那个。

sentences.en: And it's like, well, I didn't mean for this to happen.
sentences.zh: 这就好像是，嗯，我不是故意让这发生的。

sentences.en: Had I known this was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我要是早知道会发生这种事。

sentences.en: You know, I absolutely would have done that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我绝对会那样做的。

sentences.en: I'm usually a very trustworthy person.
sentences.zh: 我通常是一个非常值得信任的人。

sentences.en: But we're not perfect people all of the time, are we?
sentences.zh: 但我们不可能一直都是完美的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, oh, well, yeah, you're talking about, yeah, putting things out online, and you're making yourself vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 是的，哦，好吧，是的，你在谈论，把事情发到网上，然后你让自己变得脆弱。

sentences.en: And I think we always have this expectation for people to be perfect and to not make mistakes and not be fallible.
sentences.zh: 我想我们总是期望人们是完美的，不犯错误，也不是会犯错的普通人。

sentences.en: And it's tricky, because even when we want to be given that grace ourselves, I think initially, when we watch other people's content, or, you know, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 这很棘手，因为即使我们希望自己能得到那种宽容，我想最初当我们看别人的内容时，或者，我不知道，

sentences.en: anything you're watching, you don't hold them to that same kind of standard, you're like, oh, why have you got it wrong?
sentences.zh: 你看的任何东西，你都不会用那种标准去要求他们，你会想，哦，你怎么弄错了？

sentences.en: I can't trust anything you're saying now.
sentences.zh: 我现在什么都不能相信你说的了。

sentences.en: It's, it's very easy to slip into that black and white thinking of, oh, you've lost all my trust, if you've done one thing that hasn't kind of matched what I've expected.
sentences.zh: 人们非常容易陷入那种非黑即白的思维中，认为“哦，你做了一件不符合我预期的事情，你就失去了我对你的全部信任”。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And, and real relationships aren't like that, are they?
sentences.zh: 而且，真实的感情关系不是这样的，对吧？

sentences.en: We have to be able to tolerate grey areas, we shouldn't have to tolerate massive red flags all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们必须能够容忍灰色地带，我们不应该总是去容忍巨大的危险信号。

sentences.en: But, you know, people can really annoy us, you know, my husband annoys me regularly, and I really annoy him regularly.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，人们确实会把我们惹恼，你知道的，我丈夫经常惹我生气，我也经常惹他生气。

sentences.en: But you have to be able to work through that and, and know that, you know, this isn't our trust that's been affected.
sentences.zh: 但你必须能够克服这些，并且知道，这并不是我们的信任受到了影响。

sentences.en: I'm just, I'm just annoying, which I am.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我只是很烦人，而我也确实挺烦人的。

sentences.en: How do you keep trust?
sentences.zh: 你该如何维持信任？

sentences.en: You kind of have to keep showing up.
sentences.zh: 你必须不断地出现。

sentences.en: And, you know, you build trust through evidence, don't you?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，你是通过证据来建立信任的，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's, you can't just expect people to trust you from the get go, you kind of have to show them that they can trust you.
sentences.zh: 你不能指望别人从一开始就信任你，你得向他们证明他们是可以信任你的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's really interesting when it comes to schools and teachers, I think.
sentences.zh: 是的，这在学校和老师身上真的很让人感兴趣。

sentences.en: So observing as a parent, the teachers that have had the most successful interactions and working relationships
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个家长去观察，那些和我的孩子有过最成功的互动和工作关系的老师

sentences.en: with my children have been those that allow the relationship to develop, that earn that truSt.
sentences.zh: 往往是那些允许关系自然发展、赢得这种信任的老师。

sentences.en: The least successful ones have been the ones that have marched in and demanded that trust and demanded
sentences.zh: 最不成功的那些则是趾高气扬地走进来，要求获得这种信任和

sentences.en: that respect up front, which is just not, it's not going to work well for us as humans, I don't think.
sentences.zh: 一开始就要求获得尊重的人，我觉得这在作为人类的我们身上是行不通的。

sentences.en: No, very much.
sentences.zh: 不，确实如此。

sentences.en: And if I even bring it back to the traitors, I think that's the value of the challenges.
sentences.zh: 如果我把它扯回《反叛者》，我认为这就是挑战的价值所在。

sentences.en: But also what's tricky is that those challenges are designed to get us working as a group, building trust, because we're helping each other in those situations, which then makes it
sentences.zh: 但同样棘手的是，这些挑战旨在让我们作为一个团队合作、建立信任，因为我们在那种情况下互相帮助，这使得

sentences.en: more challenging at the round table to doubt someone if they've helped you earlier that day, for instance.
sentences.zh: 如果在当天早些时候有人帮过你的话，在圆桌会议上再去怀疑某人就会变得更有挑战性。

sentences.en: That's so true.
sentences.zh: 太对了。

sentences.en: And it's like every psychology away day that you've ever been on, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就好像你参加过的每一次心理拓展团建活动一样，不是吗？

sentences.en: Build this thing out of marshmallows and breadsticks, like it's that kind of vibe.
sentences.zh: 用棉花糖和面包棒搭出这个东西，就是那种氛围。

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it works though.
sentences.zh: 不过它确实管用。

sentences.en: I think we scoff at the team building, but we often come away from those days actually feeling closer to our colleagues, feeling bonded, and it works.
sentences.zh: 我想我们对团队建设嗤之以鼻，但我们经常从这些活动中离开时，真的会觉得和同事更亲近了，建立起了纽带，它确实有效。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: And also because when you've got, I mean, I don't know if you've ever had to transition
sentences.zh: 而且还因为当你拥有，我的意思是，我不知道你是否曾经历过将一段友谊

sentences.en: a friendship from workplace to real life, but work can point you at a specific task and then give you those kind of parallel shared experiences.
sentences.zh: 从职场过渡到现实生活，但工作可以指派给你一个具体的任务，然后给你提供那种并肩作战的共同经历。

sentences.en: Whereas sometimes there's magic in the small talk, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 然而有时闲聊中也蕴含着魔力，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which you do get away days and team building and kind of when you're under pressure or just outside of a normal environment.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过团建活动、团队建设以及当你处于压力之下或只是身处正常环境之外时获得这种魔力。

sentences.en: So the normal environment would be the castle.
sentences.zh: 所以正常的环境就是城堡。

sentences.en: You get to see more nuance to people, I think, don't you?
sentences.zh: 我想，你会对人有更细致的了解，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: It gives you a chance to get to know them in greater capacity and you stop doubting them.
sentences.zh: 这给了你一个更全面了解他们的机会，然后你就不再怀疑他们了。

sentences.en: It was a really nice break from being paranoid to just focus on a shared goal.
sentences.zh: 不用再多疑，只需要专注于一个共同的目标，这真是一个非常好的喘息机会。

sentences.en: But yeah, it did make it a lot more challenging to then pick apart who was a traitor because then
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，这确实让后来去挑出谁是反叛者变得更具有挑战性，因为

sentences.en: you're looking at behaviour in the team building going, well, who ran for a shield?
sentences.zh: 你在回顾团建时的行为会想，嗯，谁去抢盾牌了？

sentences.en: Why did they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: And then you're reinterpreting everything everyone's done.
sentences.zh: 然后你就在重新诠释每个人做过的一切。

sentences.en: You know, I remember poor Sam, like he was a faithful, had gone and got a shield because he was worried.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我还记得可怜的山姆，他是个忠诚者，因为担心而去拿了一个盾牌。

sentences.en: But ultimately, I remember thinking, actually, I think that's traitorous behaviour.
sentences.zh: 但最终，我记得自己当时想的是，其实我觉得那是叛徒的行为。

sentences.en: I think you're faking it, you know, and you get in a real loop about things.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你在伪装，你知道的，你会在这件事上陷入不断的胡思乱想。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: Oh, I mean, the ethics of it are just something else, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 哦，我的意思是，其中的伦理道德简直是另一回事，不是吗？

sentences.en: What we're doing to people.
sentences.zh: 我们对人们做的事。

sentences.en: But hopefully it's a contained enough experience.
sentences.zh: 但希望这只是一种足够可控的体验。

sentences.en: It doesn't leak too much over into your normal life.
sentences.zh: 它不会过多地渗透到你的正常生活中。

sentences.en: Did you find yourself thinking, are you telling me the truth when you left the castle?
sentences.zh: 当你离开城堡时，你会发现自己在想“你对我说的是实话吗”？

sentences.en: Well, I think I, you know, luckily with Ross being a faithful and me being a faithful, I think we were luckily in a situation where we hadn't had to lie to each other extensively
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，你知道的，幸运的是罗斯是个忠诚者，而我也是个忠诚者，我想我们很幸运地处于这样一种情况：我们不需要彼此严重地撒谎，

sentences.en: because that could have put a lot of pressure on our relationship.
sentences.zh: 因为那可能会给我们的关系带来巨大的压力。

sentences.en: I, you know, I do wonder how like the partners and friends and family of traitors feel when they watch them do really
sentences.zh: 我，你知道的，我确实在想，反叛者的伴侣、朋友和家人在看他们把游戏

sentences.en: well at the game and then they come back into their real life and go, wow, I didn't know you could lie that well, but you know.
sentences.zh: 玩得很好然后回到现实生活中时会有什么感觉，他们会说，哇，我不知道你这么会撒谎，但你知道的。

sentences.en: Oh, to be a fly on the wall in those conversations, right?
sentences.zh: 哦，真想旁听一下那些对话，对吧？

sentences.en: And I think when we're thinking psychologically, AI is such a big topic at the moment.
sentences.zh: 而且我想当我们从心理学角度思考时，人工智能是当下一个如此热门的话题。

sentences.en: How do we begin to trust AI?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何开始信任人工智能？

sentences.en: How do we begin to not over trust AI?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何做到不过度信任人工智能？

sentences.en: I don't know whether trusting AI is the goal.
sentences.zh: 我不知道信任人工智能是否是我们的目标。

sentences.en: I think working with it realistically, probably understanding its limitations
sentences.zh: 我想比较现实地与它合作，大概是理解它的局限性，

sentences.en: and kind of thinking about how transparent it's being with you and not expecting more of it.
sentences.zh: 并考虑它对你有多透明，而不要对它抱有过多期望。

sentences.en: It is a tricky question, but thank you for kind of running with that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个棘手的问题，但谢谢你顺着这个话题聊下去。

sentences.en: And, you know, people as they go through health systems are seeing more and more kind of non-human approaches, even for kind of assessing things and kind of outcome measures.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，人们在经历医疗系统时，看到了越来越多非人类的方法，甚至用于评估事物和结果衡量标准。

sentences.en: Sometimes people are not even going anywhere near, you know, a practitioner, a psychologist, a therapiSt. They're doing it all with AI or all
sentences.zh: 有时人们甚至根本不会去找执业医师、心理学家、治疗师。他们完全是用人工智能或者

sentences.en: with kind of computerized prograMs. Like that is a lot of truSt. Is that still trust?
sentences.zh: 完全依靠计算机程序来做这些。这需要投入大量的信任。这依然是信任吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, I think people are putting their trust in it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我想人们确实把信任寄托在它身上。

sentences.en: And I think that's why education around AI is so important.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么关于人工智能的教育如此重要。

sentences.en: I saw a great discussion online about someone who was using an AI chatbot as their therapist and they wanted to transition from you talking to their real therapist to just using
sentences.zh: 我在网上看到过一个很棒的讨论，关于有人用人工智能聊天机器人当作他们的治疗师，他们想从和真正的治疗师交谈过渡到只使用

sentences.en: the AI chatbot.
sentences.zh: 人工智能聊天机器人。

sentences.en: And someone wrote a great reflection on the idea that, you know, AI chatbots, you know, they're constantly available to you.
sentences.zh: 有人对此写了一篇很棒的反思，大意是，你知道的，人工智能聊天机器人，它们随时随地为你服务。

sentences.en: They're not going to challenge you.
sentences.zh: 它们不会挑战你。

sentences.en: And part of the therapeutic work is to be challenged and to go through kind of difficult times with your therapist to get to, you know, do the work, get through something.
sentences.zh: 而治疗工作的一部分就是接受挑战，与你的治疗师一起经历困难时期，从而去完成工作，度过难关。

sentences.en: And so what's complicated is the AI chatbot's never going to tell you to go away, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以复杂的地方在于，人工智能聊天机器人永远不会叫你走开，对吧？

sentences.en: Like it's giving us a false expectation of, you know, how much other people should be available to us.
sentences.zh: 就像它给我们造成了一种错误的期望，即其他人应该有多少时间可以陪伴我们。

sentences.en: And it can also, I think when we're talking about that conflation of confidence and accuracy, you know, often AI will produce results and it will tell you this is the answer.
sentences.zh: 而且它还可能，我想当我们谈到自信和准确性的混淆时，你知道的，人工智能经常会产生结果，并告诉你这就是答案。

sentences.en: And you, and you have to have the working knowledge that actually that could be wrong, even if it's saying it in a very confident way.
sentences.zh: 而你，你必须具备实际的工作知识，即实际上这可能是错的，即使它以非常自信的方式说出来。

sentences.en: It's tricky education, education, education, education, we need to understand that even when AI is telling you something is definitive, you have to go and check.
sentences.zh: 这真是个棘手的教育问题，教育，教育，教育，我们需要明白，即使人工智能告诉你某事是绝对的，你也必须去核实。

sentences.en: You do.
sentences.zh: 你确实得这么做。

sentences.en: And I fell foul of that when it gave me a route from Euston station to get to a studio location and told me it was just a simple six minute walk.
sentences.zh: 我在这上面吃过亏，当时它给了我一条从尤斯顿车站到工作室地点的路线，并告诉我这只是一段简单的六分钟步行路程。

sentences.en: And when I, when I arrived at Euston station, it was pouring with rain.
sentences.zh: 而当我到达尤斯顿车站时，外面正下着倾盆大雨。

sentences.en: It told me it was six minutes.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我那是六分钟。

sentences.en: I thought, okay, right, we're committed.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，没错，我们已经开始进行了。

sentences.en: Um, and then it turns out, no, no, no, actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后结果发现，不，不，不，其实并不是。

sentences.en: Oh yes, I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我弄错了。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: It's actually
sentences.zh: 实际上是

sentences.en: And I arrived at the studio completely dripping, soaked through, like dripping on their carpet.
sentences.zh: 我到达演播室时浑身湿透，湿得透透的，水还在他们的地毯上滴答。

sentences.en: It was, it was not my finest hour.
sentences.zh: 那可真不是我最风光的时候。

sentences.en: So yeah, let's, let's not use blind trust in our AI is what I would say.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我的建议是，别对我们的AI盲目信任。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, when I'm working as a researcher and, you know, when, I think when you're using AI in your own discipline and you really understand, you've built
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，当我作为一名研究人员在工作时，当你在自己的专业领域使用人工智能，并且你真正理解它，随着时间的推移不断积累了

sentences.en: up the knowledge over time, I can then see all the failings in the output.
sentences.zh: 知识，我就能看出它输出内容中的所有缺点。

sentences.en: I can see all the limitations, but when I use an AI chat bot to ask it something that I don't know much about, the answer sounds completely reasonable to me.
sentences.zh: 我能看到所有的局限性，但当我使用AI聊天机器人去询问一些我不太了解的事情时，它的回答听起来对我都完全合情合理。

sentences.en: And I think that really illustrates the difference is that when you, when you have expertise, you can see that it's not, it's not producing great output all of the time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真正说明了区别所在：当你拥有专业知识时，你能看出它并非总能产生优质的输出。

sentences.en: Yeah, because it, it, it can't, um, until you, I guess, really train it or really get it to get focused or to kind of, I guess, this is where it gets tricky as well,
sentences.zh: 是的，因为它做不到，嗯，除非你，我猜，真正训练它或者真正让它集中注意力，或者说，我猜，这也是它变得棘手的地方，

sentences.en: to kind of mimic the voice or the sound or the likeness of the opinion of, of someone else.
sentences.zh: 去模仿别人的声音、语调或者观点倾向。

sentences.en: Um, I know that if I was to use chat GPT as my therapist, I would, I think become quite narcissistic because it thinks I'm amazing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道如果我把ChatGPT当成我的治疗师，我想我会变得相当自恋，因为它觉得我太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very complimentary, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，它非常爱赞美别人，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I think that can be risky.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这可能会有风险。

sentences.en: Yes, it can.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实会。

sentences.en: It's almost like it's love bombing you constantly.
sentences.zh: 这简直就像它一直在对你进行“轰炸式示爱”。

sentences.en: And that's another thing to be mindful of, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这也是需要注意的另一件事，对吧？

sentences.en: With people, if people are being excessively nice to us all the time, I think it should make us think whether they actually are as trustworthy as they might seem.
sentences.zh: 如果现实中有人总是对我们好得过头，我认为这应该让我们思考他们是否真的像表面上看起来那么值得信赖。

sentences.en: Very much so.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What's it trying to do there?
sentences.zh: 它在那儿到底想干什么？

sentences.en: Constantly complimenting us.
sentences.zh: 不断地称赞我们。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's one to watch for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得这绝对是一个需要防范的现象。

sentences.en: Your work as a researcher, Ellie, must absolutely have depended on people telling you the truth or you feeling like they were telling you the truth.
sentences.zh: 艾莉，你作为研究人员的工作，肯定非常依赖于人们对你说实话，或者让你觉得他们说的是实话。

sentences.en: How do you navigate that in psychology?
sentences.zh: 在心理学中，你是如何处理这一点的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，对。

sentences.en: Where do I start?
sentences.zh: 我该从哪里说起呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So yeah, with like, I think when I am interviewing someone for research, I have to think about the pressure they might be under to give me the answers they think I want to hear.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，比如，我认为当我为研究采访某人时，我必须考虑到他们可能承受的压力，从而给出他们认为我想听的答案。

sentences.en: So that's a really important thing to consider when you're doing research.
sentences.zh: 所以这是做研究时一个非常重要的考虑因素。

sentences.en: And you do everything you can to try and encourage an honest and psychologically safe environment.
sentences.zh: 你会尽你所能去鼓励营造一个诚实且心理上安全的环境。

sentences.en: And you would do that, you know, before you ever start talking to the participant or the user, you know, in the way that you even lay out the research,
sentences.zh: 你会在开始和参与者或用户对话之前就这么做，你知道的，甚至在设计研究的方式上，

sentences.en: the information you share ahead of time, the consent you get from your kind of participant,
sentences.zh: 你提前分享的信息，你从参与者那里获得的同意，

sentences.en: you need to say like, it's okay, you know, to express yourself and not here to judge what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 你需要表明，没关系，你知道的，你可以表达自己，我不是来评判你所说的话的。

sentences.en: You also need to let them know what's going to happen to the information.
sentences.zh: 你还需要让他们知道这些信息将会如何处理。

sentences.en: That's really important.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要。

sentences.en: You know, how anonymous they're going to be in the process, because a lot of people will
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们在整个过程中会有多匿名，因为许多人会

sentences.en: worry that, you know, if they share something negative, that may have a consequence later down
sentences.zh: 担心，如果他们分享了什么负面的东西，这可能会在以后带来后果

sentences.en: the line, you know, if you're working for an organisation, they think is someone going to hear
sentences.zh: ，如果你为某个组织工作，他们会想，会不会有人听到

sentences.en: about that I said this, and am I going to lose like a benefit or, you know, something.
sentences.zh: 我说过这些话，我会不会因此失去福利或者别的什么东西。

sentences.en: So you have to be really clear about how you're operating, how your ethics are laid out, you know, you have to be as transparent as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须非常明确你的运作方式、你的伦理规范是如何设定的，你知道的，你必须尽可能地透明。

sentences.en: And even then, you're still going to get people not being wholeheartedly honest with you, maybe because they don't feel comfortable, maybe because they
sentences.zh: 即便如此，你仍然会遇到人们对你不完全坦诚的情况，也许是因为他们觉得不自在，也许是因为他们

sentences.en: haven't even, they're not even, they wouldn't even be comfortable to kind of acknowledge that to themselves.
sentences.zh: 甚至都没有、甚至不会感到自在去对自己承认这一点。

sentences.en: You know, there's, there's a lot going on, it depends what you're asking, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，情况很复杂，这取决于你在问什么，不是吗？

sentences.en: So I don't think we can eliminate the idea that people might not tell you the whole truth, in research or in other settings.
sentences.zh: 所以我不认为我们能排除人们不会对你讲全部实话的可能性，无论是在研究中还是在其他环境中。

sentences.en: But we can try as hard as we can to make it a safe environment to encourage them to.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以尽最大努力营造一个安全的环境来鼓励他们说真话。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's what the consequences would be of being completely truthful, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，完全坦白会有什么后果，这才是关键所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, I think even when I've been working in employed services as a psychologist, you know, if I'm
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我想即使在我作为心理学家在受薪服务机构工作时，如果我

sentences.en: completely truthful about everything, I might not get to keep you as my psychologist anymore.
sentences.zh: 对所有事情都完全坦白，我可能就无法再让你继续当我的心理学家了。

sentences.en: And actually, I'm really, really valuing this work that I'm doing with you.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我非常非常珍视我和你一起进行的这项工作。

sentences.en: So, you know, maybe I'll just make out that I'm a little bit less good so that I can get a properly enmeshed experience of this work
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，也许我会假装自己没那么好，这样我才能和你一起获得真正深度交融的治疗体验，

sentences.en: with you and, and feeling feeling better and making progress in the way I feel hopefully, in a lasting way, because that's what we want.
sentences.zh: 并且感觉好转，在我的感受上取得希望是持久的进展，因为这正是我们想要的。

sentences.en: We want people to be free of distress in a way that helps them live better lives, ultimately.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，我们希望人们摆脱痛苦，以一种帮助他们过上更好生活的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that's so tricky when you talk about services, and obviously, you're working to
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得谈论医疗服务时情况非常棘手，显然，你的工作

sentences.en: a remit where, you know, you might only be able to offer people that service if they meet certain
sentences.zh: 遵循一定的范围，你知道的，你可能只有在人们满足某些标准时才能向他们提供该服务，

sentences.en: criteria, and then once they're out of it, unfortunately, they then have to move on, even if what would be best for them to continue seeing you.
sentences.zh: 而一旦他们不符合了，不幸的是，他们就不得不离开，即使继续看你对他们才是最好的。

sentences.en: And then I think in when we talk about research, we'll often give incentives for someone to take part in a research session, like they might get some money.
sentences.zh: 然后我认为在讨论研究时，我们经常会给参与研究的人一些奖励，比如他们可能会得到一些钱。

sentences.en: And so the way we try and combat that is, you know, because they'll want to take
sentences.zh: 所以我们试图应对这种现象的方法是，你知道的，因为他们会为了赚钱而想参与

sentences.en: part in the research to earn the money, and then they might think that they have to say certain things or stay through the whole session, even if they're uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 研究，然后他们可能会觉得自己必须说某些话或者坚持参加完整个环节，哪怕他们感到不舒服。

sentences.en: And so what we try to do is like, maybe give the incentive right at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以我们尝试的做法是，把奖励放在最开始发放。

sentences.en: So we're like, you could leave the session after five minutes, you've still been paid for your time.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就相当于说：你可以在五分钟后离开这个环节，你的时间依然得到了报酬。

sentences.en: But it's not a perfect system.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一个完美的系统。

sentences.en: That is so important.
sentences.zh: 这太重要了。

sentences.en: And thank you for bringing that up.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你提出这一点。

sentences.en: Because ethically, yeah, I think that does matter.
sentences.zh: 因为在伦理上，是的，我认为这确实很重要。

sentences.en: And when people are listening to this podcast, perhaps thinking about their own research, I don't think I'd ever really consider what time to give that reward.
sentences.zh: 当人们在听这个播客时，也许会思考他们自己的研究，我想我以前从未真正考虑过应该在什么时候发放这种奖励。

sentences.en: And I think upfront is safest psychologically.
sentences.zh: 我认为从心理学角度来看，提前发放是最安全的。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's absolutely going to set your study up, I think, for the beSt. Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这绝对会为你的研究打下一个最好的基础。是的。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, when we're looking at many of the ways that people might be involved in psychology, sometimes litigation is part of that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，当我们审视人们参与心理学的许多方式时，有时诉讼也是其中一部分。

sentences.en: And it reminds me when I was working with people with traumatic brain injuries, there's actually whole tests that are
sentences.zh: 这让我想起我以前和创伤性脑损伤患者工作时，实际上有一整套测试

sentences.en: designed to work out whether someone is faking good or faking bad, or, you know, a really terrible term called malingering.
sentences.zh: 旨在弄清楚某人是在假装表现良好还是假装表现糟糕，或者，你知道的，有一个非常糟糕的术语叫做诈病。

sentences.en: And so just having the knowledge that actually there are, you know, a battery of tests that you can use to help work out, you know, I don't know if you've ever done an
sentences.zh: 所以，只要知道实际上有，你知道的，一整套测试你可以用来帮助弄清楚——我不知道你是否曾和某人做过

sentences.en: outcome measure with someone and, and it's like, all fours or all five, you know, across the board,
sentences.zh: 结果测量，结果全是四分或全是五分，你知道的，在所有项目上都是如此，

sentences.en: and you're like, Hmm, that is quite unusual that someone would fall would score, you know, really, really highly on every single measure.
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，嗯，一个人在每一个测量指标上都得分非常非常高，这其实挺不寻常的。

sentences.en: So when I see that, I'm often like, Oh, okay, I wonder what that's about.
sentences.zh: 所以当我看到这种情况时，我通常会想，哦，好吧，我不知道这代表着什么。

sentences.en: Or, or conversely, you know, I don't know about you.
sentences.zh: 或者，反过来说，你知道的，我不知道你怎么想。

sentences.en: But during the pandemic, I feel like people got a bit more anxious, and people got a bit more lower in mood.
sentences.zh: 但在大流行期间，我觉得人们变得更加焦虑了，人们的情绪也变得更加低落。

sentences.en: And so even when we would begin to kind of complete the GAD seven, or the PHQ nine, or screening measure like that, we wouldn't expect to have a zero score.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使在我们开始填写GAD-7、PHQ-9或类似的筛查量表时，我们也不会期望得到零分。

sentences.en: Because actually, there's a lot of stress in the modern day world that you would be in, you'd be tripping up.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，现代世界中有很多压力，你不可避免地会受到影响。

sentences.en: So when you're getting complete negatives on things, but that can be a sign, I think, to ask more questions.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你对所有事情都得到完全否定的回答时，我认为这可能是一个需要提出更多问题的信号。

sentences.en: Yeah, very much so.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And if I think back to my time working in assessment services, like autism assessment, ADHD assessment, I was an assistant psychologiSt. And, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果我回想我在评估服务部门工作的时光，比如自闭症评估、ADHD评估，我曾是一名助理心理学家。而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: we understand that it's such a long journey to get to your assessment date, and you may have formed your own opinions about what's going on for you.
sentences.zh: 我们理解，走到评估日期是一段非常漫长的旅程，你可能已经对自己的状况形成了自己的看法。

sentences.en: And you will may have you may be invested in a certain outcome.
sentences.zh: 而且你可能对某个特定的结果有所投入和期待。

sentences.en: And that might be a diagnosis or something.
sentences.zh: 那可能是一个诊断结果或别的什么。

sentences.en: And it can be really, really challenging to unpick, you know, what's actually going on for someone, you know, versus how they feel what they
sentences.zh: 要剥丝抽茧地弄清楚，你知道的，某人身上到底发生了什么，与他们的感受、他们

sentences.en: think is going on versus maybe what you know, the clinical psychologist would kind of surmise is going on.
sentences.zh: 认为发生了什么，或者也许与临床心理学家推测发生的情况相比，这可能会非常非常具有挑战性。

sentences.en: And it's just really challenging.
sentences.zh: 这真的极具挑战性。

sentences.en: And kind of I can see it from all perspectives, you know, you've been alone for a long time, you've had to work things out.
sentences.zh: 而且我能从各个角度理解这一点，你知道的，你独自煎熬了很长时间，你不得不自己去解决问题。

sentences.en: And you've kind of gone, this is it.
sentences.zh: 然后你差不多会得出结论：情况就是这样。

sentences.en: And then it can be a much more complex conversation when you actually get into the assessment process.
sentences.zh: 接着，当你真正进入评估过程时，这可能会变成一场更为复杂的对话。

sentences.en: Yeah, it can indeed.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And even telling people we're a psychologist
sentences.zh: 甚至告诉别人我们是心理学家

sentences.en: can get people's hackles up.
sentences.zh: 都会让人心生戒备。

sentences.en: And they think that we're mind readers, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们以为我们能读懂心思，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I get that a lot.
sentences.zh: 我经常遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: But I think I'm right in saying you didn't tell people you were a psychologist when you went into the castle.
sentences.zh: 但我想我没记错的话，你进城堡时并没有告诉别人你是心理学家，

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: No, I didn't.
sentences.zh: 是的，我没说。

sentences.en: Because I didn't want them to preform any opinions.
sentences.zh: 因为我不想让他们预先形成任何看法。

sentences.en: And so I was actually telling everyone I was a nanny.
sentences.zh: 所以我实际上告诉所有人我是一个保姆。

sentences.en: Which I didn't, I didn't think it made the final cut.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这部分并没有被剪进最终的正片里。

sentences.en: And ultimately, it wasn't important.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这并不重要。

sentences.en: And actually, all that did for me was put more pressure on myself, because then I was having to kind of I have worked as a nanny previously.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我这么做只是给自己施加了更多压力，因为接下来我不得不——我以前确实当过保姆。

sentences.en: So I was drawing on real experience, but I wasn't currently working as one.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在借鉴真实的经验，但我当时并不是在从事这个职业。

sentences.en: So I was kind of having to like slightly make up this, you know, this is what I'm doing as a nanny now.
sentences.zh: 所以我有点像是在半编造这个身份，你知道的，“这就是我目前作为保姆在做的事”。

sentences.en: And I was like, this is really distracting from actually playing the game.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，这太分散我玩游戏的注意力了。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think people make lots of assumptions about psychologists.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，我认为人们对心理学家有很多刻板印象。

sentences.en: And only half of them are right.
sentences.zh: 而且只有一半是对的。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But I can I can quickly see why you were just having this whole like, narrative that must have been making your head spin and trying to almost remember what you have,
sentences.zh: 但我能、我能很快明白为什么你脑子里会一直转着这样一整套说辞，一定让你头晕目眩，还要努力去记住你对别人

sentences.en: and you haven't told people, which must just made your time so much more challenging.
sentences.zh: 说过什么、没说过什么，这一定让你的那段经历变得更加充满挑战。

sentences.en: I have to say,
sentences.zh: 我必须得说，

sentences.en: Ellie, having met you having spent time with you, I would like to correct the judgment of you as being bland, the most bland contestant.
sentences.zh: 艾莉，在见到你、与你相处之后，我想纠正对你的那种评价，即认为你是乏味的、最乏味的参赛者。

sentences.en: I thought that was so mean.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那太刻薄了。

sentences.en: I don't think that should have been able to be asked of anybody that felt unjuSt. And I would say it's not fitting of you at all.
sentences.zh: 我不认为应该对任何人提出这种要求，这让人感觉很不公平。而且我要说，这根本不符合你的性格。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I mean, I understand that those challenges are designed to provoke, you know, so I get why they do it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我理解那些挑战的设计就是为了挑起矛盾，你知道的，所以我明白他们为什么要这么做。

sentences.en: And I also understand that because I was holding back so much information from my fellow players, I was giving them a very bland version of me.
sentences.zh: 我也理解，因为我对其他玩家隐瞒了太多信息，我展现给他们的是一个非常乏味版本的自己。

sentences.en: I wasn't talking to them about my relationship, about my work, about anything.
sentences.zh: 我没有跟他们谈论我的感情关系，没有谈论我的工作，没有谈论任何事。

sentences.en: I was just going.
sentences.zh: 我只是在过日子。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that that's probably quite interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得这可能挺有趣的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because actually, when we do make relationships with people, it's based on us being a bit invested, I think.
sentences.zh: 因为事实上，当我们与人建立关系时，它是建立在我们投入了一定情感的基础上的。

sentences.en: And if it all feels just like business, then you feel like this person hasn't really got a foot properly in the relationship.
sentences.zh: 如果这一切感觉都只是公事公办，你就会觉得这个人并没有真正全身心地投入到这段关系中。

sentences.en: So maybe that's what they were kind of picking up on is that it felt a little bit one sided, or there wasn't, you know, you weren't a multi dimensional person, because
sentences.zh: 所以也许这就是他们当时所察觉到的，那就是感觉有点单方面，或者缺乏，你知道的，你并不是一个多维度的人，因为

sentences.en: clearly, you weren't saying I've got a boyfriend called Ross, he's great, like, because that would have thrown you under the bus.
sentences.zh: 很显然，你没有说“我有一个叫罗斯的男朋友，他很好”，因为那样的话你就会把自己给出卖了。

sentences.en: Yeah, very much so.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And you know, I understood before going into the castle, that group bonding was really important to this game.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在进入城堡之前，我明白团队凝聚力对这个游戏非常重要。

sentences.en: But the reality was, I put all these kind of barriers in place for myself, not really thinking this through, about how I was going to bond with the group,
sentences.zh: 但现实是，我给自己设置了所有这些障碍，却没有真正想清楚我要如何融入这个集体，

sentences.en: because actually, yeah, I'd really limited myself there about what I could talk about.
sentences.zh: 因为事实上，是的，我在能谈论的话题上真的对自己进行了太多限制。

sentences.en: Well, I have loved talking with you, Ellie.
sentences.zh: 好吧，和你的谈话我非常喜欢，艾莉。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来参加我的节目。

sentences.zh: 我们的听众可以在哪里了解更多关于你和你的工作？

sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间，作为一个可爱、体贴的嘉宾，和我们一起探讨关于信任的话题。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.zh: 再次感谢我的嘉宾抽空前来，

sentences.zh: 艾莉·巴克利博士。

sentences.zh: 你们觉得呢？
